name: Minimal / Modern
description: Reduction to the fewest shapes that still read instantly. The subject is a confident silhouette with one or two deliberate details; emptiness is an active design element.
visual_characteristics: 3-6 shapes carry the whole subject; every element earns its place
negative space >= 40% of the canvas; subject sits on a considered off-centre or optical-centre anchor
one dominant colour + one accent + neutral; no decorative texture
quiet precision: aligned edges, shared radii, shared angles

palette.guidance: Off-white or deep ink base, one saturated accent, one soft neutral. Max 4 colours in total. Colour is used to guide the eye to a single focal point.

geometry: Primitives (circle, rect, rounded rect, arc, simple polygon) on a hidden 8- or 12-unit grid. Shared corner radius across the piece. Curves are true arcs or clean quadratic curves, never wobbly. Prefer 45/90 degree angles.
stroke: Either fill-only or one uniform stroke weight (2-4% of canvas) with round caps and joins. Never mix more than two stroke weights.
texture: None. No noise, no grain, no patterns.
composition: Rule of thirds or true centre with generous margins (>= 10%). One focal point. Asymmetric balance through scale contrast (big shape vs tiny accent). Align to a baseline.
typography: If text is needed: one geometric or grotesque sans, 1-2 sizes, generous tracking on small caps, aligned to the grid. Prefer converting to paths for logos.
lighting_depth: Flat. Depth only by overlap and scale; optionally one soft cast shadow shape at low opacity, never a blur filter.
svg_techniques: author on a 0 0 512 512 (or 1024) grid; snap coordinates to multiples of 8/16
use <circle>/<rect rx>/<path> arcs; build symmetry with <use> and a mirror transform
define palette as CSS custom properties or one <style> block for easy recolouring
use clip-path to trim shapes instead of drawing complicated paths
as_secondary: acts as a REDUCTION MODIFIER: cut the primary's detail ~60%, keep 3-4 colours and >=40% negative space, but retain ONE signature technique of the primary (e.g. a single neon edge, one line of ornament).

name: Flat Design
description: Solid-colour shapes with no outlines, gradients or realistic shading. Depth comes from overlap, colour value steps and long or offset shadow shapes.
visual_characteristics: solid fills only; shading is done with a second, darker or lighter flat shape
friendly simplified proportions; rounded rectangles and circles dominate
bright but harmonised palette of 5-8 colours with clear value steps
clear layering: background, mid shapes, character/object, small props

palette.guidance: Curated 5-8 colour palette; each hue gets one light and one dark step. Keep saturation consistent; use one warm and one cool family.

geometry: Simplified geometric anatomy: circles for heads, rounded rects for bodies. Consistent corner radius. Edges are hard; shapes tile without gaps. Minimal curves; clean bezier arcs.
stroke: None by default (fill-only). If lines are needed for detail, use one weight, round caps, in a darker tone of the fill rather than black.
texture: None. Optionally a very sparse dot or diagonal-line accent for one area.
composition: Scene built in 3 depth planes. Central subject with supporting props at varied scale. Use overlapping to imply depth and keep a clear focal contrast.
typography: Rounded or geometric sans, bold weights, high legibility. Short labels only.
lighting_depth: Implied light from top-left: one darker flat 'shade' shape per object, occasionally a long flat shadow at 45 degrees (a parallelogram path). No blur, no gradients.
svg_techniques: one <g> per object, palette via CSS variables
shadow shapes created by clipping a duplicate with clip-path (define once, <use> repeatedly)
long shadows as polygons with fill-opacity .12-.2
no filters at all

name: Geometric
description: The subject is constructed from a small vocabulary of mathematical primitives on a visible or hidden construction grid; rhythm, symmetry and proportion do the storytelling.
visual_characteristics: circles, triangles, squares, arcs and lines only - sometimes 1-2 special forms (quarter circles, lens shapes)
strict proportion system (golden ratio, root-2, or a modular grid)
repetition, rotation and mirroring create rhythm
hard edges, exact tangencies, no organic wobble

palette.guidance: Limited palette (3-6) with strong value separation; alternate warm/cool between adjacent shapes so every boundary reads.

geometry: Every shape derives from a documented grid (state it in a comment). Arcs share centres; triangles are equilateral or right isosceles; angles are multiples of 15 degrees. Overlaps use even-odd cut-outs.
stroke: Prefer fills. If lines are used they are constant-width, butt caps, miter joins for crispness.
texture: None, or a repeated geometric pattern (dots, hatch) as its own tiled shape.
composition: Centred or radially symmetric or strict modular grid. Balance through repetition and scale steps. Leave consistent gutters.
typography: Constructed geometric caps drawn from the same primitives, or a geometric sans.
lighting_depth: Flat. Depth via overlap and transparency (multiply-like overlaps by explicit intersection colours).
svg_techniques: <pattern> or <use> loops for repetition; rotate <use> around a centre for radial symmetry
explicit intersection shapes via clip-path for overlap colours instead of mix-blend-mode
comment the grid unit at the top; compute coordinates from it
fill-rule="evenodd" for concentric cut-outs

name: Monochrome
description: One hue (or pure black on white) carries everything. Form, depth and focus are built purely from value, line weight, pattern density and negative space.
visual_characteristics: a 4-7 step value ladder from paper to darkest ink
contrast planned so the focal point holds the strongest value jump
line weight and hatching density replace colour as the variable
silhouette must work in pure black

palette.guidance: Choose ONE hue (or neutral) and derive 4-7 tints/shades of it by lightness only; keep saturation constant. For duotone add a second ink and use it sparingly.

geometry: Any geometry that suits the subject, but built from large clear value masses first, then edge detail. Shapes have soft or hard edges consistently within the piece.
stroke: Line weight variation is the main expressive tool: thick for silhouette/contours, thin for interior detail. Round caps, round joins.
texture: Hatching, stippling or halftone patterns to create mid-values without introducing new colours.
composition: Value-block first: 3 masses (dark, mid, light). Strongest contrast at focal point; darks connected into a readable shape; leave paper white for highlights.
typography: Single family; weight contrast (light vs black) for hierarchy.
lighting_depth: Strong single light source; cast shadows are the darkest value; atmospheric depth by lightening distant forms.
svg_techniques: define value steps as fills (or one fill with varying fill-opacity over a paper base)
<pattern> for hatch / dots at 2-3 densities
group by value layer (highlights / mids / darks) for editability
stroke-width variety through separate <path> layers, not filters
avoid: gradients that muddy the value ladder
using opacity on multiple stacked shapes so values become unpredictable
as_secondary: acts as a PALETTE CONSTRAINT: keep the primary's structure but recolour everything to a single hue's value ladder (or black/white). Lighting and texture of the primary are expressed through value only.

name: Luxury / Premium
description: Restraint plus precision: dark or ivory grounds, hairline geometry, metallic gradients used sparingly, and generous emptiness that signals confidence.
visual_characteristics: very deep base (near-black, midnight, oxblood) or warm ivory
metallic accent (gold/champagne/rose gold) as thin lines and small masses, never large flat areas
symmetry, fine ornament, precise margins
small number of elements with impeccable alignment

palette.guidance: Near-black or ivory base; metallic gradient accent (3-4 stops from deep gold to pale champagne); one muted secondary (emerald, oxblood or navy). No bright saturated colours.

geometry: Symmetrical, centred, on a strict grid. Thin double rules, fine arcs, small diamond/lozenge ornaments. Monoline construction.
stroke: Hairline (0.5-1.5% of canvas) with butt or round caps; double rules with a gap; metallic stroke via linearGradient.
texture: Optional very subtle fine grain or micro-pattern at <= 5% opacity; or none.
composition: Centred axis, tall margins, small mark with lots of air; type spaced widely. Key element sits slightly above the geometric centre (optical centre).
typography: High-contrast serif (Didone/Garamond-like) or thin wide-tracked sans caps; small sizes, tracking +150..+300. Fall back to generic serif; outline text for logos.
lighting_depth: Flat with metallic gradients that imply a light sweep (diagonal, 3-4 stops); no heavy shadows.
svg_techniques: define a reusable <linearGradient id="gold"> with userSpaceOnUse coordinates so the sweep is consistent across shapes
use stroke="url(#gold)" for hairlines
mask a subtle diagonal sheen across the main mark
keep <text> letter-spacing generous and convert to paths for the final logo
as_secondary: acts as a SURFACE FINISH: keep the primary's structure, but move to a near-black or ivory base, thin the strokes, and introduce metallic gold-gradient accents on 1-3 hero elements only.
